conventions: Import-robustness vectors (TEST §5.1, T-DIC-001, T-DIC-011…T-DIC-015): each case is a zip built from "zip.entries" and imported like any Yomitan zip (DIC-001), into "dicts_dir" (default dicts) of a temporary folder, from "zip.file" (default <id>.zip). The zip is written field by field, so it can hold what no zip library writes: entries are in order, each one "name" (UTF-8) or "name_hex" (raw bytes), with its uncompressed content as "json" (written compact), "text", "hex", "noise" ({size, seed}: Fushi's xorshift64 bytes, x = seed * 0x9E3779B97F4A7C15 + 1, then for each byte x ^= x << 13, x ^= x >> 7, x ^= x << 17 and the low byte of x) or "template" ({text, count, separator, prefix, suffix}: text with {i} replaced by 0…count-1, joined). "method" is "stored" (default) or "deflate" (raw deflate, level 6); "compressed" replaces the compressed bytes ({"noise": …} or {"hex": …}); "corrupt" changes them: "half" keeps the first half, "first-64" the first 64 bytes, "scramble" maps every byte b to (b ^ 0xA5) + 0x13, "invert" to !b. "declared_size" is the uncompressed size written in both headers (default the real one); "flags" the general purpose flags (bit 11 = 2048: UTF-8 name); "extra_hex" the extra field of both headers; "zip64" lists the central directory fields written as the 0xFFFFFFFF sentinel, with their real values in a 0x0001 field ("size", "compressed_size", "offset", always in that order). The CRC-32 fields hold the real checksum of the content (Fushi's fixtures write 0, which its own zip reader ignores). "expected.error" means the import fails, with the kind of error: the message id of the error without "error-dict-" ("zip", "no-index", "format", "empty"…), "unsafe:<reason>" for an entry refused by DIC-011 (TooLarge, Bomb, Traversal…), or "any"; a failed import must leave nothing in the dictionaries folder (DIC-013). Otherwise the import succeeds and: "title" is index.title; "kinds" the types of DIC-015 (term, kanji, frequency, pitch); "counts" some of the counts of the import (terms, term_meta, kanji, kanji_meta, tags, media, frequencies, pitches); "styles" the styles.css kept, exactly; "media" maps a path, looked up as the popup looks it up, to its bytes in hex, to {"entry": name} (the content of that zip entry) or to null (no such media); "terms" maps an expression to the glossaries of its terms, in order. "damage" lists changes to the dictionary file after the import ({"truncate": n} or {"at": offset, "hex": bytes}); "expected.survives" then lists expressions: opening the damaged file and looking each up must return, with a result or an error, within 30 s and without a panic. "divergence" marks a case where a Nikomiru requirement differs from Fushi: "expected" follows the requirement and the divergence's "fushi_expected" is what Fushi gives, in the same shape. "known_failure" marks a case that fails today because of the file named by "owner": the runner expects it to fail, and fails when it passes, so that the mark is removed. "skip" marks a Fushi case that cannot be expressed (internal APIs, MDX, process-level cases ported elsewhere); the note says why or where it went. "provenance.test" names the Fushi case: its comment or assertion labels. The cases come from the assertions of the Fushi tests, without a run of Fushi's code; where a Fushi test checks less than a case (an exact title, a media path), the rest follows the Nikomiru requirements and the note says so.
